Article Title: iPhone Fold, Pro and Pro Max: Apple’s biggest 'iPhone gamble' in years gets a launch date
Article Text:
Apple could do for foldables what it has done before

Where will the regular iPhone go

Apple has sent invites for its 'September event'. iPhone-makers 'Surprise and shine' event is set for September 9. Apple September iPhone event is usually the most predictable date on the technology calendar. New iPhones arrive, the Pro models get the biggest upgrades, cameras improve and prices are debated. This year could be very different.If reports around Apple's 2026 plans are accurate, the company could use its September event for arguably the biggest restructuring of the iPhone portfolio in years. Two changes stand out: Apple is expected to finally enter the foldable smartphone market, while the regular iPhone 18 may not launch alongside the Pro models at all.That would leave the September lineup dominated by Apple's most expensive phones — the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and its first foldable iPhone. The standard iPhone 18 is instead expected to arrive in spring 2027.And all of this is happening just as the smartphone industry enters an uncomfortable new era of higher hardware prices.Apple will be arriving extremely late to foldables. Samsung has been selling them since 2019, while Google, Oppo, Honor and others have spent years solving problems around hinges, durability, thickness and screen creases.Yet foldables remain a niche category, accounting for less than 3% of global smartphone sales. That is precisely why Apple's arrival matters.The company has repeatedly entered categories after rivals and then helped push them towards the mainstream. The Apple Watch was hardly the first smartwatch, nor were AirPods the first wireless earbuds. Apple's strength lies in taking an existing idea, making it easier to understand and putting it in front of a huge installed base. IDC has forecast global foldable smartphone shipments to grow about 30% in 2026, driven significantly by Apple's entry. Counterpoint has separately projected a 20% increase.For Samsung, this creates both an opportunity and a problem. Samsung executives have publicly welcomed Apple's expected entry, arguing that another global player will expand the category. There is logic to that: Apple could effectively validate a form factor Samsung has spent seven years on and has also largely succeeded.But Samsung also risks losing something important — ownership of the foldable conversation. Until now, a premium book-style foldable has largely meant Galaxy Z Fold. Apple entering the category changes that. Also, Apple is unlikely to compete on price. Current expectations put the first foldable iPhone above $2,000, with some estimates stretching towards $2,500. That could make it one of the most expensive mainstream smartphones Apple has ever sold. Oddly, that price may help rather than hurt its strategic purpose. Apple does not need the Fold to become the biggest-selling iPhone immediately. It needs the device to create excitement at the top of the portfolio and establish a new premium tier above the Pro Max.The second change may be less glamorous but equally important. Apple is reportedly splitting its iPhone launch cycle. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected in September, alongside the foldable, while the regular iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e could move to spring 2027.For consumers, that means something unusual: there may be no new "vanilla" iPhone at Apple's biggest hardware event of the year. For Apple, however, the strategy makes considerable sense.The September event would become an unapologetically premium showcase. Instead of a $799-ish entry point sitting beside far more expensive devices, attention would remain on models carrying the highest margins and biggest technological upgrades.It could also smooth Apple's sales cycle. Rather than concentrating nearly the entire iPhone launch in one quarter, Apple can create another major upgrade window six months later. But there may be another reason why separating cheaper and expensive iPhones suddenly makes sense: RAMageddon.AI-driven demand for memory is pushing DRAM and NAND prices sharply higher. IDC says memory can account for 15-20% of the bill of materials of a mid-range smartphone and 10-15% of a flagship. It expects manufacturers to respond by increasing prices, cutting specifications or doing both.Apple itself is reportedly examining cost reductions for the regular iPhone 18, including cheaper display specifications and changes to chips and components, as RAM costs rise. It is part of a much broader smartphone trend. Oppo, Vivo, Realme, OnePlus, Samsung and others have already begun raising prices in India as memory and component costs increase. Qualcomm, too, is raising processor prices from September.Premium phones are better placed to absorb those increases because component costs represent a smaller proportion of their selling price. Which makes Apple's expected September strategy particularly interesting. At precisely the moment when smartphones are becoming more expensive, Apple may be removing its mainstream model from its biggest launch and doubling down on the expensive end. September 2026 could therefore be remembered not simply as the year Apple finally made a folding phone. It could be the moment the iPhone itself became a more deliberately premium product.
Article Summary: Apple is expected to finally enter the foldable smartphone market. The regular iPhone 18 may not launch alongside the Pro models at all. That would leave the September lineup dominated by the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and its first foldable iPhone. The standard iPhone 18 is instead expected to arrive in spring 2027.

Article Title: Operation Bluebird startup launches Twitter.now, says it is not linked to Elon Musk's X
Article Text:
Operation Bluebird launches Twitter.now (AI-edited image)

A startup sees an opportunity after Twitter became X

A judge's comments gave the startup confidence to launch

Here’s what Operation Bluebird co-founder wrote on LinkedIn

The name Twitter has returned to the internet. A Virginia-based startup called Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now, claiming that the Twitter name and some of its well-known intellectual property were abandoned after Elon Musk renamed Twitter to X. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. Operation Bluebird says its platform is not connected to X and is building a different kind of online public square, with automated fact-checking and more control for users over what they see.When Elon Musk acquired Twitter in 2022, he eventually renamed the platform X and replaced the familiar blue bird branding. Operation Bluebird believes that decision created an opportunity to reclaim the Twitter name.The startup's co-founder Stephen Coates, who previously served as general counsel at Twitter before Musk's takeover, said the company had waited for months before launching but did not want to delay further.Operation Bluebird's legal argument is that X Corporation abandoned its rights to trademarks linked to Twitter, including the word "Twitter," "tweet" and the bird logo. X Corporation, however, sued Operation Bluebird last year and sought to stop the new platform from launching.The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.Legal dispute between Elon Musk’s X and Operation Bluebird continues.During an April 2026 hearing, US District Court Judge Colm Connolly gave a tentative ruling suggesting that X appeared to have given up its intellectual property claims over the word "tweet" and the Twitter bird logo. The judge also raised the possibility that rights to the word "Twitter" may have been abandoned.However, the judge has not yet issued a written order.The move could now intensify the legal battle. Trademark attorney Josh Gerben told Ars Technica that Operation Bluebird may have a workable legal argument, but said the case was far from straightforward and that X could respond strongly now that the platform has launched.In a LinkedIn post, Coates wrote:"Today, Operation Bluebird launched Twitter.now.When X Corp. retired the Twitter brand, we saw an opportunity to build something new: a public square organized around trust, transparency, and user choice.Twitter.now is not an attempt to recreate the old platform. We are building a different service, with trust signals that provide context for what users see and tools that allow people—not an opaque algorithm—to decide how much credibility and noise reach their feeds. Our governing principle is simple: freedom of speech, not freedom of reach.Twitter is a reclaimed brand. We are not X and are not affiliated with X Corp.Early access is now open. Founding members can help us build and test the platform, get first shot at the handle of their choice, and claim their place in its history—including Founder number #00001.The public square is open again, and definitely not affiliated with X in any way. Whatsoever.Get over your X. The bird is back."
Article Summary: Virginia-based startup Operation Bluebird has launched a new social media platform, Twitter.now. The launch comes despite an ongoing legal fight with X Corporation, which has challenged the startup's attempt to use the old Twitter identity. The legal dispute is still ongoing, and a final decision has not been issued.

Article Title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' event on September 9: Foldable iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro and everything else to expect
Article Text:
The foldable iPhone is the biggest launch expected on the day

The iPhone 18 Pro upgrade sounds modest, the price rise may not be

Watches, AirPods and new home devices make up the rest of the list

Siri AI is the software behind most of these new devices

Apple has confirmed September 9 for its annual iPhone launch, and the invite sent out on Wednesday uses the tagline "Surprise and shine." The keynote starts at 10am Pacific, which is 10.30pm IST, and will stream from the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple Park via Apple's site, YouTube and the Apple TV app.Two things separate this from the usual September routine. It is the first Apple event with John Ternus running the company, since Tim Cook hands over the CEO title on September 1 and becomes executive chairman. The rumoured product list is also unusually long. Apple pushed the new Mac mini and Mac Studio out in late August, a slot it has used only once in the past decade, and several reports read that as an attempt to free up space on stage.The device drawing the most attention is Apple's first foldable, which most reports expect to be called iPhone Ultra. Leaks point to a 7.8-inch inner display that opens like a book and a roughly 5.3-inch cover screen, with the A20 Pro chip and 12GB of memory.Rumours suggest two 48MP rear cameras and no telephoto lens, which would be an odd omission at this price. There are also claims that authentication falls back to Touch ID rather than Face ID.Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, who says he has spoken to people who have used the phone, reports that the hinge and the way it fits in a pocket both impressed them, and that it works well as a camera viewfinder. He expects pricing to start above $2,000, roughly Rs 1.8 lakh before Indian duties, so the local figure would likely be higher.The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are widely tipped as a spec-bump year. Reports point to a 2nm A20 Pro with packaging changes meant to help thermals, Apple's own C2 modem, a slightly larger camera bump and a dark cherry finish. A variable-aperture rear camera is rumoured to be a Pro Max exclusive, and under-display Face ID has been floated without much backing.Pricing is the bigger question. With memory costs climbing, Samsung and Google have each raised phone prices by about $100, and Gurman expects Apple to follow, which would put the iPhone 18 Pro near $1,199. Other estimates run steeper.The standard iPhone 18, the iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air are not expected in September, with reports pointing to 2027.Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a light update, with talk of a health sensor tied to a fluoroelastomer band, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 may get a redesign. AirPods 5 look likely, in ANC and non-ANC versions. The camera-equipped AirPods that leaked in a macOS Tahoe release candidate are still reported as a 2027 product.The home devices are the bigger unknown. Reports mention a refreshed Apple TV 4K, a new HomePod mini and a home hub with a seven-inch screen. Gurman reports Apple is reworking the accessory sections in its retail stores, which he takes as a sign of more than routine updates. An OLED iPad mini remains a wildcard.Most of the home hardware has reportedly been waiting on the Siri overhaul Apple previewed at WWDC in June. That keynote was structured differently from the usual run through each operating system in turn, with Apple instead laying out a cross-platform pitch built around Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.The version demoed uses large language model technology to let the assistant act inside apps such as Messages and Calendar rather than only answering questions. It is the feature Apple has been promising and delaying since 2024.Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Tahoe, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27, reportedly in the back half of September and initially as a waitlisted beta. That timing matters for the hardware. A refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini would need newer chips to support it, which is one explanation for why those updates have taken so long, and a home hub with a screen makes little sense without an assistant that can act on requests.
Article Summary: Apple will launch the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max on September 9. The foldable phone is expected to start at around $2,000. Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods are expected to be light updates. Siri AI is expected alongside iOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27 and tvOS 27.

Article Title: Apple pitches Mac mini, Studio for the age of local AI
Article Text:
Apple Mac mini

New Delhi: Apple is making a stronger pitch for the Mac as a local AI computing machine, positioning its new Mac mini and Mac Studio as systems capable of running AI models, automated workflows and agentic workloads without relying entirely on the cloud.TOI spoke to Apple and learned that “desk-side” AI compute is emerging as a key use case, as developers and enterprises increasingly look to run language models and AI workflows locally instead of sending every task to large cloud-based systems.The shift is important because the AI boom has so far been dominated by hyperscale data centres packed with expensive GPUs. But as models become more efficient and desktop hardware gets more capable, a growing number of AI workloads can be handled locally, particularly for development, testing and inference.Apple is looking to tap into this transition through its unified memory architecture and tightly integrated hardware and software stack. The company is pitching Macs as machines that can keep more AI workloads on-device, potentially reducing dependence on cloud infrastructure while also offering advantages around latency and data privacy.The new Mac mini comes with either Apple’s M6 or M5 Pro chip. Apple says the M6 version delivers up to four times faster AI performance and twice the graphics and storage performance compared with the previous generation.It starts with 16GB unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, while the M5 Pro version supports up to 64GB. The machines also get Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and faster Ethernet, while Thunderbolt 5 on the M5 Pro model allows multiple Mac minis to be clustered together to run larger AI models locally.The Mac mini with M6 starts at Rs 99,900 in India, while the M5 Pro version starts at Rs 2,09,900. Both will go on sale from September 22.At the higher end, the new Mac Studio comes with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips and is aimed at developers, AI researchers, data scientists and creative professionals. Apple claims up to 4.3 times faster AI performance, along with faster graphics and storage. The M5 Ultra version can be configured with up to 512GB of unified memory, allowing significantly larger AI models to be loaded and run locally.Mac Studio with M5 Max starts at Rs 2,79,900, while the M5 Ultra model starts at Rs 6,29,900. The 512GB configuration will be available later in October.Apple’s broader bet is that the Mac can carve out a role in an AI computing stack that increasingly combines cloud, edge and local processing — not replacing massive GPU servers, but serving as a powerful desk-side system for building, testing and running increasingly capable AI workloads.
Article Summary: Apple is positioning its new Mac mini and Mac Studio as systems capable of running AI models, automated workflows and agentic workloads without relying entirely on the cloud. Apple says the M6 version delivers up to four times faster AI performance and twice the graphics and storage performance compared with the previous generation.

Article Title: Microsoft introduces Xbox Disc-to-Digital program allowing players to turn their game discs into digital version
Article Text:
How the conversion process works

Cloud gaming and cross-platform integration

Microsoft has introduced a new programme under which console owners can turn their physical game discs into digital versions, essentially ‘modernising’ collections built over several console generations. The disc-to-digital program, previously revealed in an exclusive report by The Verge last month, forms a core part of Microsoft’s broader video game preservation strategy as the company prepares its hardware ecosystem for future console generations.According to the company, the functionality will support the vast majority of disc releases across both Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles. Jason Ronald, vice president of Next Generation at Xbox, explained that players can unlock their digital entitlement by inserting a compatible disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.The digital license remains tied to the physical media itself. If a user trades the disc with a friend or signs in under a different profile, the entitlement transfers accordingly to the current player holding the physical copy. Activating the digital version does not alter the physical disc, which continues to function normally in compatible disc drives.The company noted that this conversion “requires supported console with disc drive, and [an] eligible XBOX One or Series X game disc.”Once converted, players unlock standard digital perks across the broader Xbox ecosystem. Supported games can be streamed to a variety of hardware via Xbox Cloud Gaming or played natively across Windows PCs through Xbox Play Anywhere.It is to be noted that Microsoft will begin testing the feature with members of the Xbox Insider community on August 31, followed by a wider public rollout across Xbox One and Xbox Series X systems in the ensuing months.“We’re starting with thousands of titles, and we’ll continue to add more over time. While not every title will be available at launch, this is an important step toward a future where players can have greater confidence that the games they buy remain with them for years to come,” Ronald said.
Article Summary: The disc-to-digital program forms a core part of Microsoft’s broader video game preservation strategy. Supported games can be streamed to a variety of hardware via Xbox Cloud Gaming or played natively across Windows PCs through Xbox Play Anywhere. Microsoft will begin testing the feature with members of the Xbox Insider community on August 31, followed by a wider public rollout in the ensuing months.

Article Title: Apple teases ‘Surprise and Shine’ event as iPhone 18 Pro, foldable iPhone likely to take centre stage
Article Text:
First ever foldable iPhone and flagship refresh expected on September 9 event

Adjusted release timelines and 2027 Apple launch roadmap

First event under New CEO John Ternus

Apple has officially announced the dates of its biggest event of 2026. The company’s next major product launch is set for September 9, according to the media invitation sent, bearing the tagline “Surprise and shine”. The showcase is set to begin at 10:30 pm IST at the Steve Jobs Theater inside the Apple Park campus, with global audiences able to watch via an official digital livestream at apple.com or on the Apple TV app.According to Mark Gurman, Apple may introduce mechanical aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Sky Blue: a possible new iPhone 18 Pro colour.The upcoming event could mark a product milestone, as expectations build around Apple potentially unveiling its inaugural foldable iPhone. Leaked photos of what appears to be a physical dummy model suggest the folding handset features a broad layout which appears to be like the recently-launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.Apple is also anticipated to introduce hardware upgrades across its high-end lineup, likely designated as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, following a redesign delivered in the previous product cycle.Reports have indicated a shift in standard product rollout schedules.The standard base-model iPhone 18 will not be unveiled during the September presentation, with the company opting to launch it next year instead, reports claimed.Moreover, Apple is rumoured to be preparing an entry-level iPhone 18e alongside a second-generation iPhone Air for introduction in 2027.The September showcase represents a major milestone for executive leadership at Apple. The presentation will serve as the first official public event led by John Ternus as CEO. Formerly serving as Apple’s hardware engineering chief, Ternus is scheduled to assume the top role on September 1, succeeding long-time CEO Tim Cook.
Article Summary: Apple has announced the dates of its biggest event of 2026. The company’s next major product launch is set for September 9. The showcase is set to begin at 10:30 pm IST at the Steve Jobs Theater inside the Apple Park campus.

Article Title: 110 years after the National Park Service was created, Google has put America's parks into a new virtual hub with more than 150 stories, 30 tours and 3D artifacts
Article Text:
Interactive exhibits and immersive features

Marking 110 years since the establishment of the National Park Service, the US National Park Service (NPS) has teamed up with Google Arts & Culture to launch the United Parks of America virtual platform, essentially bringing the country’s natural landscapes and historic landmarks directly to global audiences. The digital initiative provides open access to the nation’s cultural heritage and preserved lands, enabling people around the world to discover iconic sites regardless of their physical location.Jessica Bowron, National Park Service Comptroller exercising the delegated authority of the Director, emphasised the importance of broad public reach.“As we celebrate our 110th birthday during National Park Week, one of our biggest priorities is access—engaging people in new ways and making sure as many people as possible can experience these special places. Working together with Google Arts & Culture allows us to share the natural wonders and historic significance of our parks with people, even those who might never get to visit in person. This collaboration ensures America’s story will endure and remain accessible to everyone,” Bowron said.The newly introduced online portal incorporates interactive digital tools to help users explore park resources in entirely new ways.For example, it features more than 150 curated stories and 30 virtual tours, helping visitors explore the majesty of America’s scenic landscapes and discover artifacts that tell the nation’s story from anywhere in the world.It also utilises technology, including 3D models, AI-powered guides and immersive storytelling, so that the public can interact with park resources in ways never before possible.The digital platform arrives as a cornerstone project for National Park Week, backed by refreshed narrative features and a joint promotional video illustrating the collaboration.
Article Summary: The US National Park Service (NPS) has teamed up with Google Arts & Culture to launch the United Parks of America virtual platform. The digital initiative provides open access to the nation’s cultural heritage and preserved lands. It also utilises technology, including 3D models, AI-powered guides and immersive storytelling.

Article Title: Australia to ban fully AI-generated songs from its official music charts after an AI track reached No. 2 and stayed in the Top 20 for 16 weeks straight
Article Text:
An old-fashioned record player plays in the office of Mikey Shulman, one of the founders of AI music generator startup Suno, Tuesday, Jan. 13, 2026, in Cambridge, Mass. (AP Photo/Robert F. Bukaty)

AI can still touch a track. It just cannot write it or sing on it.

ARIA can pull a chart position and take back a No. 1 award later

Australia's official music charts will stop counting songs built entirely by artificial intelligence. The Australian Recording Industry Association has rewritten its Charts Code of Practice, and the change kicks in with the ARIA chart dated August 31. Songs that use AI as a helper are still welcome. Songs where the machine did the actual creative work are out, and ARIA says the point is to "promote the human nature of artistry" in what it calls the most crowded market artists have ever had to fight through.The timing is not a coincidence. A version of Madonna's Like a Prayer by Queensland DJ Josh Fawaz, made with AI-generated vocals and drums, has spent 16 weeks in the Australian top 20. It peaked at No. 2 in May, was still sitting at No. 4 this week, became the most-played track on Australian radio and has crossed 48 million streams on Spotify alone. Fawaz described AI as a tool and added generative AI credits to the listing only after the criticism started.The new bar is specific. A recording qualifies only if "humans wrote the song and performed the lead vocal and the primary instruments," ARIA said.Mastering, drum machines and auto-tune are all still fine. Anything using generative AI has to be substantially human made, has to be produced with licensed AI services, and must raise no stream or chart manipulation concerns. Artists now declare their AI use when they submit a song.Enforcement runs backwards as well as forwards. ARIA can refuse an entry, remove a recording in advance or retrospectively, redo chart positions, withdraw accreditations and revoke an ARIA No. 1 Award, including asking for the trophy back. AI-generated tracks are also locked out of the ARIA Awards. Artists and their representatives can contest an exclusion and submit evidence that a track clears the rules.Australia is following a template, not writing one. The rules come from principles the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry published in July, which more than 20 official chart programmes are adopting, with rollouts across Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia. Sweden pulled an AI-made song from its charts earlier this year. ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd has asked Australian radio to write similar rules of its own, which is the real test given how the Fawaz track spread.That track, by ARIA's own reading, probably would not clear the new bar. It just cleared the old one for four months first.
Article Summary: Australian music charts will stop counting songs built entirely by artificial intelligence. The change kicks in with the ARIA chart dated August 31. A version of Madonna's Like a Prayer by Queensland DJ Josh Fawaz, made with AI-generated vocals and drums, has spent 16 weeks in the Australian top 20.

Article Title: Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI, which US government accused of ‘stealing’ Anthropic's tech, may make revenue deals with Microsoft, Amazon and Google
Article Text:
A booth for Chinese AI Startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 during the World AI Conference in Shanghai

How deal between Chinese company and US tech giants may look like

Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup Moonshot AI is reportedly in preliminary negotiations with American technology giants Microsoft, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud to establish revenue-sharing partnerships for hosting its frontier Kimi K3 model. This is the same AI model that the White House accused the startup of using stolen Anthropic technology to build – the very model that knocked down tech stocks earlier this year.Citing people familiar with the discussions, news agency Reuters reported that the talks reflect rising Western demand for top-performing Chinese machine learning systems, which frequently provide competitive performance at significantly lower price points than Western counterparts. If finalised, the arrangements would represent the first significant commercial revenue-sharing pact between a domestic Chinese AI lab and premier US cloud infrastructure providers.According to the report, Moonshot is seeking up to a 30% share of proceeds generated from Kimi K3 deployments hosted on Microsoft Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, matching the commercial terms it proposes to major enterprise clients.Reuters says that its sources note that discussions remain in early phases without guaranteed outcomes, with negotiators working through unresolved questions surrounding data access permissions, token audit protocols and exact revenue splits.As Kimi K3 features a massive 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight architecture, few corporate clients can absorb the immense computational hardware costs required to run the model on private on-premise servers, making public cloud distribution vital for widespread enterprise adoption.In benchmark testing by Arena.ai, Kimi K3 ranked first in web interface creation, while evaluation platform Artificial Analysis reported that the system performs on par with OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 in executing intricate, multi-step problem solving.
Article Summary: Moonshot AI is reportedly in preliminary negotiations with American technology giants Microsoft, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud to establish revenue-sharing partnerships. This is the same AI model that the White House accused the startup of using stolen Anthropic technology to build – the very model that knocked down tech stocks earlier this year.

Article Title: In 1962, IBM built a secret NSA computer that ran jobs up to 200 times faster than any other machine; 14 years later a worn-out part ended its run because its maker was no longer in business
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

IBM built Harvest as a specialised NSA computer

Harvest processed large volumes of intercepted data

“Moretown,”

“It was quite an amazing computer,”

“One instruction, for example, could do sorts, and do statistical analysis of the data that was streaming by it.…

Everything we were doing at that time was on the cutting edge. There was no question about it.”

“It’s beautiful, but it doesn’t work.”

IBM built Tractor to keep Harvest supplied with data

Harvest had its own programming language

“scab,”

“pad,”

“I spent the good part of a summer on that,”

“And it just disappeared into Fort Meade somewhere.”

“Bureau of Ships.”

Harvest remained in use as newer computers arrived

“conceived in the fifties, born in the sixties, and irreplaceable in the seventies.”

“I first began operations at NSA. Although not widely known, I was probably the largest, fastest, and most technically advanced computer system in the world,”

“And now, fourteen years later, the time to retire has come. The cost of my upkeep and operation has been overtaken by more modern equipment and the newer technologies.”

The NSA replaced Harvest with the Cray-1

IBM built a secret computer for the US National Security Agency that began operating in 1962 and remained in service for 14 years, processing some of the agency's most sensitive cryptographic workloads during the Cold War. Known as Harvest, the machine could run certain jobs up to 200 times faster than other computers of its time, according to accounts of its capabilities.According to a report by IEEE Spectrum, Harvest finally stopped running on February 27, 1976, after a mechanical component in its automated tape library wore out. The manufacturer of the part was no longer in business, leaving the NSA without a practical way to replace it. By then, the machine had operated through the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Vietnam War, and the period leading up to the 1975 Helsinki Accords.Harvest was officially designated the IBM 7950 and was built around IBM's 7030 Stretch mainframe. IBM developed Stretch for scientific computing, but the NSA needed a system that could continuously process large volumes of intercepted communications without requiring operators to manually stage each batch of tape.After two unsuccessful proposals, IBM secured the NSA contract in 1958. The resulting system combined Stretch with a custom streaming processor and an automated tape-storage system called Tractor.Unlike a general-purpose computer, Harvest's custom processor was designed to repeatedly apply a fixed sequence of operations to data streams. It could take two streams, known as P and Q, from memory, process them and return the result as a third stream, R.The processor used overlapping stages, or a pipeline, so that while one pair of data bytes was being processed, the next could already be fetched from memory. Harvest shared memory with Stretch and could address individual bits rather than being restricted to complete bytes or words.Its processing units included a logic unit for bitwise operations and a table-lookup unit that could use incoming data to address information in memory.The NSA used Harvest for cryptanalytic and large-scale text-processing jobs. One documented example described the machine searching 3.5 billion characters of text for any of 7,000 target terms in just under four hours.Another job, referred to asinvolved searching 11 million messages covering 16 years of intercepted traffic against about 8,000 search terms. NSA analyst Robert Looney said in 1972 that the job took about 10 hours, although he did not disclose the purpose of the search.As a complete system, Harvest could stream one byte every 0.3 microseconds and had about 800 kilobytes of addressable memory.IBM engineer Frances Allen, who worked on both Stretch and Harvest, later recalled the type of operations the machine could perform.Allen said in a 2001 oral history.Harvest's specialised design also created challenges within the NSA. According to James Bamford's 2001 history of the agency, some officials reportedly looked at the machine during employee tours and said,The system nonetheless continued to handle large jobs that general-purpose machines were not well suited to process.Harvest's processing capacity required a storage system that could supply large datasets without constant human intervention. IBM therefore built Tractor, an automated magnetic-tape library officially designated the IBM 7955.Each Tractor cassette weighed about 6 to 7 kilograms and contained roughly 120 megabytes of data on a 550-metre reel of tape. Each storage unit could hold up to 160 cassettes.When Harvest began operating in 1962, three automatic cartridge units were connected to it, each serving two tape drives. Together, they provided about 44 gigabytes of online storage.The automated system used a motor-driven arm to retrieve cassettes from storage racks and deliver them to tape drives. The mechanism could move at about 6 metres per second, while software running on Stretch controlled cassette movement and data reading and writing.Moving from one completed tape to the next could take about 18 seconds, once the next cassette had been retrieved and was ready to mount. Retrieving and preparing a cassette did not require manual handling.Tractor therefore functioned as both long-term storage and a source of data for Harvest's processing jobs. Conventional reel-to-reel drives connected to Stretch were also used when large datasets had to be transferred into or out of the system.IBM and the NSA also developed a programming language specifically for Harvest. Called Alpha, short for Advanced Language for Programming Harvest, it was designed around the machine's streaming architecture and the needs of cryptanalysts.Alpha allowed programmers to define the alphabet used for cryptographic data and included symbols for representing uncertain or null characters. Arepresented by a question mark, indicated a character that was known to exist but whose identity was unknown. A blank space represented aor null character.The language also provided ways to combine strings into larger structures, giving programmers a way to describe complex intercepted messages and cryptanalytic datasets.Allen worked on the Harvest software and later recalled that the technical report she produced for her part of the project disappeared into the NSA's classified system after she completed it.she recalled in 2001.Harvest's secrecy also shaped how some IBM employees understood the project. Allen said the NSA was not widely known outside classified intelligence circles when she began working on the machine, so she initially believed she was working on a naval project. The budget code name for the NSA wasBy 1971, Harvest was operating about 115 hours a week, according to Looney, representing more than two-thirds of its available operating time. At the same time, the number of jobs it handled had been declining since 1967 as newer general-purpose computers took over ordinary data-processing work.Harvest was increasingly reserved for large, specialised workloads that other machines could not handle as efficiently.At the system's 10th anniversary in 1972, Looney described it as a machineThe description did not last much longer.On February 27, 1976, operators shut Harvest down for the final time. A mechanical component in the Tractor tape library had worn out, and the company that manufactured the part was no longer operating. Replacing the system's ageing hardware was no longer practical.The NSA marked the occasion with a mock telegram written in Harvest's name.it said.The NSA eventually replaced Harvest with the Cray-1 supercomputer. Unlike Harvest, the Cray-1 used newer integrated circuits and was designed primarily for numerical and scientific computing, but its processing capabilities also made it suitable for workloads that had previously required Harvest's specialised hardware.The Cray-1 was also commercially available to multiple customers, unlike Harvest, which had been built specifically for the NSA. As newer general-purpose and scientific systems improved, maintaining a custom machine for one specialised workload became less practical.Harvest did not have a direct line of successors, partly because its architecture was built around the NSA's particular requirements. Several of its concepts, however, appeared later in other areas of computing.Tractor's automated tape library anticipated robotic storage systems later used in large data centres. Harvest's pipeline architecture also resembled approaches that became part of dataflow computing, while its continuous pattern-matching operations have parallels in later systems designed to inspect network traffic.Harvest's operational life ended with a worn mechanical part and an unavailable manufacturer, but the ideas used to build the system continued to appear in computing systems developed after it.
Article Summary: IBM built a secret computer for the US National Security Agency that began operating in 1962 and remained in service for 14 years. Known as Harvest, the machine could run certain jobs up to 200 times faster than other computers of its time. One documented example described the machine searching 3.5 billion characters of text for any of 7,000 target terms.

Article Title: America's richest techies' new status symbol is a Swiss watch, and Sam Altman ordered seven worth over $1 million with these words engraved on them
Article Text:
Sam Altman's OpenAI watch: seven made, over $1 million (Credit: Vanguart)

What's actually engraved on Sam Altman's OpenAI watch

Vanguart engraved 'SCALING' on the crown pusher and 'COMPUTE IS DESTINY' around the rotor of the OpenAI watches

Vanguart is tiny even by Swiss watchmaking standards

OpenAI's Tudor watch is the version mortals can chase

Why company-logo watches now resell above retail

Silicon Valley has run through a lot of flexes. The hoodie. The Tesla. The Cybertruck parked outside a Palo Alto bungalow worth eight figures. The latest one is smaller, quieter and sits on the wrist. It is also the most expensive thing most of these men own that is not real estate. And Sam Altman has taken it further than anyone else in tech.The OpenAI chief executive commissioned seven custom watches from Vanguart, a Swiss maker that has been around for barely eight years, according to a Wall Street Journal report. They were built for a handful of hand-picked OpenAI staff, and the engraving reads less like watchmaking and more like an in-joke from a research lab. The order was based on Vanguart's titanium Orb, a model that starts at $180,000—which puts seven of them past the million-dollar mark before customisation. Altman declined to comment through an OpenAI spokeswoman.Wind the watch and you'll find "COMPUTE IS DESTINY" running around the rotor in capitals, a line attributed to Altman himself. The crown pusher carries a single word—"SCALING". Flip it over and the caseback reads if AGI.aligned: deploy(), written in Python, rendered in colour on the movement, the way code looks inside an editor with syntax highlighting on.It also has "LIMITED OpenAI" stamped around the rim. And, there's an OpenAI logo on the dial.That last one was suggested by Axel Leuenberger, Vanguart's CEO and co-founder. Company chairman and co-founder Mehmet Koruturk told the Journal the line is about AI being put to peaceful use. OpenAI's knot logo sits at 12 o'clock as an applied, openworked piece, roughly where a brand name would normally go. Hands and hour markers glow a pale green, and the flying tourbillon spins away in the open at 6 o'clock with no dial covering it.Underneath the styling is a serious watch. The Orb runs 41mm across and 10.5mm thick in grade 5 titanium, with a movement of 395 components, 35 jewels and about 60 hours of power reserve. Switching between automatic and manual winding is done through the crown, and in automatic mode a titanium orbital mass set with a 2mm diamond circles a track on the dial side, appearing to float.Roughly a third of Vanguart's 33 employees worked on the OpenAI commission, Koruturk said. For scale: Audemars Piguet has more than 3,000 staff and turns out about 50,000 watches a year. Vanguart has made fewer than 200 in its entire existence. In the US, its ready-made pieces are sold at exactly one address—Material Good in SoHo.Hidden details are a house habit. Koruturk told the Journal the brand aims for "subtle tributes embedded for those who know where to look."Not every OpenAI watch costs as much as an apartment. Boris Power, the company's head of applied research, posted on X that Tudor—Rolex's sister brand—made 400 watches carrying the OpenAI logo on the dial, with "Good Research Takes Time" on the back, a slogan OpenAI has also printed on T-shirts.And OpenAI is far from alone. Business Insider reported that Palantir staff got a run of 468, an Uber engineer posted a model numbered 1/100, and Google's version used the Tudor Pelagos, which retails around $4,500. These aren't gifts from HR. They're organised by employee collector groups, who round up enough buyers to hit Tudor's minimum order of 40, then wait about six months. Everyone pays full retail.At Adobe, product designer Georgia Benjamin is working with British watchmaker Studio Underd0g on a 128-piece run at around $1,200 each, for employees only. Benjamin, who owns about 40 watches, described the appeal as belonging to an insider club.The secondary market has noticed. Eric Ku, co-founder of online auction house Loupe This, sold an Amazon-branded Tudor earlier this year for $8,250. A Tudor Black Bay 54 customised with Meta's logo has drawn bids as high as $10,500—a standard version with a metal bracelet retails for $4,725. Business Insider reported that a Google Tudor featuring the Chrome dinosaur went past $10,000 at auction, while an Apple "pirate" edition pulled a $13,500 bid. Ku's read is simple: collectors chase the unusual. He also warned that plenty of branded pieces flop—people sometimes just find them ugly.None of this is new territory for tech's biggest names. Mark Zuckerberg has worn a $1.3 million F.P. Journe. Altman's collection includes a Greubel Forsey that ran to roughly $650,000. What's changed is the flex itself—less about what the watch cost, more about the logo on the dial telling you where its owner works.
Article Summary: OpenAI chief executive commissioned seven custom watches from Vanguart, a Swiss maker that has been around for barely eight years. They were built for a handful of hand-picked OpenAI staff, and the engraving reads less like watchmaking and more like an in-joke.
